slides.headline: On Venus, a day is longer than a year
slides.subline: **It sounds impossible.** It isn’t. Swipe for the numbers.
slides.credit: NASA/JPL / Public domain (Venus, Magellan radar data)

slides.body: Venus circles the Sun in about [[225 Earth days]]. But it spins once in about [[243 Earth days]]. One full turn takes **longer than its year**.
Venus spins **backwards** compared with most planets. The Sun rises in the [[west]] and sets in the east. Sunrise to sunrise takes about **117 Earth days**.
The surface is about [[465°C]], hot enough to melt lead, even though Mercury is **closer to the Sun**. Thick clouds trap the heat.
The air pressure on Venus is about **90 times** Earth’s. Which planet would you most want to visit? Tell us below.
